r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: PASS on every constraint the handoff names. (i) Guard not widened into a check that cannot fail: proven two ways -- the permissive mutation drives 9 failures (k2), and the name-only decoy is rejected while a real bundle and a NAME-FREE bundle are both accepted (k1), so the predicate discriminates in both directions. The probe fallback is the frozen plan's specified behaviour, not the forbidden widening: the predicate still returns False for the checkout and the worktree. (ii) Fail visibly, no silent fallback: the note IS emitted -- I separated the streams and confirmed it lands on STDERR ('note: this script is not inside an installed bundle ...; resolved installed skills root ...') while stdout carries only the ok line. (iii) The note is for a human, not a check: nothing in the change makes a command condition depend on it, and the implementer surfaced the engine-discards-stdout limitation as a triage candidate rather than building a check on it -- correct handling. (iv) Targeted tests plus the relevant broader suite: 11 targeted tests / 17 subtests plus the eight-file coupled suite, no no-test-surface exception claimed. (v) Test naming contract honoured: the three-location matrix and the decoy carry guard_location, the wrong-root test carries guard_mutation, and I verified on this machine that a zero-match selector exits 5, so both floors are real.

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json, run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py <record> (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command ships with a C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/epic418-w5-gates/.agent-work/w5-gates/g1-review/fowler-pass.json placeholder; record() runs that command and refuses `pass` while it fails. NORMAL PATH -- resolve the placeholder to the real record path when you INSTANTIATE this survey from the template, before you claim: it is an instantiation-time substitution exactly like w5-gates on line 2. That is the documented route and the one you should be on. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record later moves or the path you substituted was wrong, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.

k1-decoy.title: CC1: name-only decoy rejected (built by reviewer)
k1-decoy.imperative: Build a constellation-<name> directory with NO SKILL.md inside a real skills root myself and confirm _is_installed_bundle rejects it. Do not accept the implementer's test as proof.
k1-decoy.finding: PASS on criterion 1 as written. I built three decoys and two controls myself (repro/decoy.py), independent of the implementer's tests. Decoy1 (constellation-decoy, NO SKILL.md, inside a CORPUS.json-marked root) REJECTED. Decoy2 (same, root marked only by clause 2 via a real sibling bundle) REJECTED. Both are name-test positives, so the old guard would have taken them. Positive control (real bundle) ACCEPTED and name-free control (totally-unrelated-name under a marked root) ACCEPTED -- so the predicate can say both yes and no, and its yes does not consult the name. OBSERVATION (not criterion 1): decoy3, a constellation-* dir carrying SKILL.md whose parent is otherwise an ordinary directory, is ACCEPTED -- because _is_skills_root's clause 2 globs 'constellation-*' in the PARENT and the candidate matches ITSELF. For a constellation-*-named candidate the parent clause is therefore vacuous and the predicate degrades to 'has SKILL.md'. No real location is misjudged by this (all three measured in k3), and the failure mode is a visible downstream refusal, not a silent accept.

k4-skills-root-wins.title: CC4: --skills-root exists and WINS over a detected bundle

consolidation.summary: APPROVE. All seven close criteria independently reproduced, not accepted. The guard is demonstrably not a check that cannot fail: I built the name-only decoy myself (rejected, while a real bundle and a name-free bundle are accepted) and the permissive mutation drives 9 failures across the guard_location selector, restored to identical blob OIDs. Both polarities fixed and measured at all three real on-disk locations, with the unfixed on-main copy as a discriminating control. --skills-root wins over a correctly-detected bundle and over a working probe. The refusal's stated count (3) parses equal to the roots actually listed. Both selectors collect nonzero unpiped, a bogus selector exits 5 on this machine, and the coupled suite is 386/480 green with the delta reconciled to the file's own method count. No blockers. Four triage candidates, the leading one a measured latent regression path: the constellation-* glob runs on the parent so the source repo self-matches, which would resurrect #501 if the repo ever gains a root-level SKILL.md.

triage_candidates.statement: _is_skills_root clause 2 is self-satisfying: for a candidate named constellation-* that carries SKILL.md, parent.glob('constellation-*') matches the candidate itself, so _is_installed_bundle's parent clause is vacuous and reduces to 'has SKILL.md'. Exclude the candidate from its own parent scan (or require a DIFFERENT sibling) to keep the structural test genuinely two-clause.

verify_explorer and verify_commander read their work-area artifact BEFORE resolving the skills root, so an invalid --skills-root is masked by an artifact-missing refusal in those two modes; only admiral-prelaunch surfaces 'skills-root is not a directory' first. Consider resolving the root before reading the artifact so the flag's own error is not shadowed.

g1-implement-RESULT.md claims the CORPUS_MARKER duplication is 'commented at both ends of the intent'; only the verifier end carries the back-reference. install_constellation.py was correctly off-limits, so if the other end is wanted it needs its own scoped change.

Nothing asserts verify_iterative_role_artifacts.CORPUS_MARKER still equals install_constellation.CORPUS_MARKER. A rename of the installer's marker would silently degrade _is_skills_root to its sibling-glob clause instead of failing. Add a one-line equality test.

MEASURED consequence of tc1 (same root cause, this is the actionable part): because the constellation-* glob runs on the PARENT, the source repo self-matches. I measured it on a temp stand-in for C:/Programs -- today _is_skills_root(Programs)=False and _is_installed_bundle(repo)=False (correct), but the moment constellation-skills gains a root-level SKILL.md, _is_skills_root(Programs) flips to True and _is_installed_bundle(repo) flips to True, resurrecting #501's wrong-accept exactly. The fix is therefore correct today but conditional on the repo never acquiring a root SKILL.md. One-line hardening: exclude the candidate itself from its own parent scan (require a DIFFERENT sibling bundle).
